This method significantly increases the file size limit:\\n\\n\\u2022 *Upload limit:* 2000 MB (2 GB) per file.\\n\\u2022 *Total payload limit:* 4000 MB (4 GB) for requests involving multiple files, like a media group.\\n\\u2022 *Premium user uploads:* A local Bot API server supports file sizes larger than 2000 MB, but only if the user uploading them has a Telegram Premium subscription. *1- Scope of platforms: web only*

• Please limit Licensed Platforms to HTML5 / WebGL browser distribution only (for example <http://CrazyGames.com|CrazyGames.com> and other web portals).

• We would like to also exclude YouTube playables and Telegram from the list. We’ll pursue those 2 web publishing paths on our own since we have good connections with the YouTube team directly and have an expert community builder on Telegram.

We are comfortable giving this a real shot, but the current structure creates a long lock-in with a long tail.
• Initial term: 12 months is fine, but we would like to add mutual termination for convenience after an initial test period. For example: after the first 3 months from launch, either party can terminate for convenience on 30 days written notice.

*3- Transferability and assignment*
We are not comfortable with a fully transferable license that can be assigned freely.
• The license should be non-transferable except to your wholly owned affiliates.
• Any assignment or transfer to a third party should require our prior written consent.
*4- Monetization and outbound links*
We understand that you control monetization on your portals, but we would appreciate some room to promote our own ecosystem. Is it possible to include links to the iOS and Android store pages for Domino Delights and Zombie Match 3D? These links can follow your UX guidelines. This is not something we’ll pursue right away but we would like to reserve the options with your consent.

*5- SDK and post termination support*
We are fine integrating your SDK and keeping it up to date during the term, but not for an extended period after termination.
• Please remove the requirement to update or re-integrate the SDK for up to one year after termination.We are happy to commit to updating the SDK during the transition period.
• Post termination, we are happy to commit to keeping the last live version stable for a short transition period (for example 60 days), with critical bug fixes only and no new features or SDK migrations.
If you can accommodate these changes, we will be in a good position to move ahead quickly. Feel free to send a revised draft, or if it is easier, we can mark up the current one and return a redline.
Best regards,

Telegram games, which are built as Mini Apps, do not have a binary size restriction because they are web applications hosted on a developer’s server, not static files uploaded to Telegram’s servers. This is a key distinction from binary files like documents or videos that users upload. However, other file size limits apply to media that a Mini App or bot might send or receive.

File size restrictions for Telegram bots and Mini Apps
Standard Bot API
If your game uses the standard Telegram Bot API to send files (e.g., images, videos, or game assets), the following file size limits apply:

• *Photos:* 10 MB maximum.
• *Other files (including game assets):* 50 MB maximum. 
• 
Local Bot API server
For developers who need to exceed the standard limits, Telegram allows running a local Bot API server. This method significantly increases the file size limit:

• *Upload limit:* 2000 MB (2 GB) per file.
• *Total payload limit:* 4000 MB (4 GB) for requests involving multiple files, like a media group.
• *Premium user uploads:* A local Bot API server supports file sizes larger than 2000 MB, but only if the user uploading them has a Telegram Premium subscription. Bots themselves cannot have a Premium account an[USERNAME_1352] therefore cannot upload files larger than 2000 MB. 
• 
Development and performance considerations
Game logic and assets
Since Mini Apps are web-based, the total size of your game is only limited by your hosting environment and browser performance. The following strategies are recommended for optimizing performance:

• *Server-side optimization:* Keep your game logic on your own server to minimize the data sent to the user.
• *Asset compression:* Compress and optimize images, videos, and other assets to reduce loading times. Tools like TinyPNG can help significantly.
• *Lazy loading:* Only load assets when they are needed, rather than all at once, to improve the initial loading speed.

Definitions
• Revenue: cash collected from Telegram users attributable to [PERSON_NAME_0133].
• Direct costs: UA on Telegram, creator payouts, refunds, chargebacks, payment processing, platform fees, promo credits, other variable costs.
• Net Profit: Revenue minus Direct costs, calculated monthly.
Tiered profit share, per month
• 20% on the first $25,000 of Net Profit
• 15% on the next $50,000 of Net Profit, i.e., $25,001 to $75,000
• 10% on Net Profit above $75,000
• Monthly cap: total payout to [PERSON_NAME_0133] cannot exceed $15,000 for that month
• Floor: if Net Profit is positive but under $5,000, pay the greater of calculated share or $500
• No payout if Net Profit ≤ 0
Why this structure
• Starts aggressive on the first dollars of profit, then steps down to 10%.
• The cap is reached at $100,000 monthly Net Profit:
    ◦ 20% of first $25,000 = $5,000
    ◦ 15% of next $50,000 = $7,500, cumulative $12,500
    ◦ 10% of next $25,000 = $2,500, cumulative $15,000 cap
Examples
1. Your scenario
• Revenue: 100,000 users × $0.50 = $50,000
• Direct costs: $10,000
• Net Profit: $40,000
• Payout: 20% of $25,000 = $5,000, plus 15% of $15,000 = $2,250, total $7,250
2. Strong month
• Net Profit: $100,000
• Uncapped math would be $16,250, but the monthly cap applies, payout = $15,000
3. Modest month
• Net Profit: $4,000
• Calculated share at 20% = $800, floor applies only if higher than share. Payout = $800
Attribution and scope
• Scope: Telegram only, assets [PERSON_NAME_0133] manages.
• Attribution: unique links or postbacks. Mixed traffic allocated by last touch on Telegram assets [PERSON_NAME_0133] controls.
• Refunds and chargebacks reduce Revenue in the period recognized.
Payment terms
• Close books on the 5th, pay by the 15th.
• Monthly report: Users, Revenue, Direct costs, Net Profit, tier math, and payout.

**Telegram DD initiative shelved — closing this master and its open sub-tickets as Canceled.**

Decision of record: the Telegram distribution push for Domino Delights was called off in January 2026. On **Jan 6, 2026**, Leonard terminated the contract with the Telegram community operator (the profit-share distribution lead) and confirmed to her that *"we changed directions and won't be doing telegram anytime soon"* (Slack, founders/product channel). The company has since moved into wind-down, and the CrazyGames web deal explicitly **excludes** Telegram (we reserved that path for ourselves but are not pursuing it).

Cleanup performed today (Feb 28, 2026) so the tracker reflects reality for the Sunset data handover:
- Canceled: ENG-2377 (this master), ENG-2380, ENG-2381, ENG-2382, ENG-2383, ENG-2385, ENG-2388 — none of this work is active or will be resumed.
- Left as Done (genuinely completed before the effort was shelved, kept for accurate history): ENG-2379 (Telegram MiniApp bot + DD integration) and ENG-2387 (Jenkins dev/prod Telegram builds).

There is no active Telegram work. Do not treat this as in-flight.

input.title: Move Domino Delights off Helpshift → email-based support
input.description:
Helpshift subscription is being terminated as part of wind-down (Leonard requested mutual early termination ~Feb 9; Helpshift agreed to cancel; all outstanding invoices paid). Cutoff to be off Helpshift: **Feb 28/29, 2026**. Decision (Leonard, winddown channel): keep it simple — replace the in-game "Contact Us" with an email-to-support flow so players can email **[support address, SVC_0293_EMAIL]** directly. No data export needed from Helpshift.

**Current state (verified in code, `harmonygames-Games/GameOfDominoes`):** NOT done. `Assets/GoD/Scripts/UI/MainGame/ContactUs.cs` — the `OpenEmailClient()` method actually calls `HelpshiftInitializer.Instance.HelpshiftSdk.ShowConversation(...)`, i.e. support still routes through Helpshift. Helpshift SDK is still initialized and the SupportUS constant still points at harmonygames.helpshift.com.

**Remaining to-dos:**
- [ ] Change Contact Us action to open the device email client (mailto to the support address) with userId prefilled in the body — replace the `HelpshiftSdk.ShowConversation` call. Applies to the World Map top bar Contact Us and the splash-screen / connection-error Contact Us added in ENG-2399.
- [ ] Remove/disable Helpshift init + unread-count red-dot polling so a dead SDK doesn't error at boot (see the splash-hang risk in ENG-2363).
- [ ] Ship a build to iOS + Android before the Helpshift cutoff.
- [ ] Confirm the support inbox is monitored during wind-down.

Owner: Arthur Blake. Created during tracker cleanup Feb 28, 2026 — this move was living entirely in Slack and was untracked.

input.description:

**Current state (verified in code, `harmonygames-Games/match3d`):** NOT done. `Assets/Scripts/UI/MainMenu/SettingsPopup.cs` and `Assets/Scripts/UI/Splash/SplashScreen.cs` still call `HelpshiftInitializer.Instance.HelpshiftSdk.ShowConversation(...)`. Helpshift SDK is still initialized; SupportUS constant still points at harmonygames.helpshift.com. (Note: PR #524 earlier added a "Contact Us / Open Email" button on the splash screen — verify whether that path is email-based or also Helpshift, and standardize all contact entry points on email.)

- [ ] Change Settings-popup and splash-screen Contact Us to open the device email client (mailto to support address, userId prefilled) — replace the `HelpshiftSdk.ShowConversation` calls.
- [ ] Remove/disable Helpshift init + settings red-dot unread polling so the dead SDK doesn't error at boot.
- [ ] Ship a build to iOS + Android before the Helpshift cutoff.
- [ ] Confirm the support inbox is monitored during wind-down.

input.text:
📋 *Wind-down rundown — eng/tracker side (Fri Feb 28)*

*1. Tracker cleanup (Linear) — done, so the export we hand Sunset is accurate*
• *Telegram:* the whole DD-on-Telegram push was called off in January (contract with the operator terminated Jan 6, "changed directions, not doing Telegram anytime soon"). The master ticket still said "In Progress" — I've *Canceled* it plus the 6 open sub-tickets, left the 2 that were genuinely finished as Done, and put a note on the master (ENG-2377) pointing at the Jan decision so nobody has to re-dig it.
• *UI Optimization sprint:* a pile of tickets were stuck in PR/Validation even though the code merged to `develop` back in Nov. Reconciled against GitHub — *flipped 14 to Done* (all Core Game + all Mini-Games + Nathan's Treasure + Axe Arena). *7 were parked in review with no code behind them* (Collect&win, River Rush, Season Pass, Remove Ad, Offers, Rate-us pop-ups, Daily Gift) — left open and flagged individually. Heads up: River Rush / Remove Ad / Offers were *ticked on the checklist but never actually merged*.

*2. Helpshift move — both games, cutoff is today; NOT done yet* ⚠️
• Vendor side is handled: termination requested, Helpshift agreed to cancel, invoices paid.
• *In-game side is NOT done.* Both DD and Zombie Match still route "Contact Us" through the Helpshift SDK (verified in code — DD's `ContactUs.cs` and ZM's `SettingsPopup`/`SplashScreen` still call Helpshift `ShowConversation`). When Helpshift access ends, that button dies.
• Plan per your note: swap Contact Us to just open the email app to our support address. That code change + a build for iOS & Android still has to happen. I've now *tracked it*: *ENG-2438* (DD) and *ZOM-2439* (ZM), both P1/due today with the exact to-dos. Realistically this ships a day or two late vs the cutoff — players briefly lose in-app support until the build lands, but no data is lost (no Helpshift export needed).

*3. Sunset data handover (tracker side — on me)*
• Linear + Trello exports into their shared drive: still owed. Linear is now cleaned up and accurate to export; I'll drop both.
• Your Slack question: *yes, exporting private channels/DMs requires the Business+ plan* (Corporate Export). On our current plan we can only export *public* channel history — so pulling these private channels needs the upgrade.
• (Figma viewer access for their side was already granted earlier.)

*4. CrazyGames deal*
• Web publishing agreement signed early Dec (web/HTML5 only — CrazyGames → MSN → FB → WeChat; Telegram & YouTube excluded). *Integration never started* — there's no CrazyGames SDK/WebGL integration work in the codebase. Their PM is following up with Robert. Needs a call: do a minimal integration or tell them we can't proceed given the wind-down. Not currently tracked in Linear.

*5. Other genuinely-open eng items*
• The 7 UI-opt Live-Ops tickets above (no code; unlikely to ship in wind-down).
• A few stray open PRs pending review (DD economy changes + tile-dozer window fix; ZM info-screen animations).
• Otherwise: Telegram is dead/cleaned, UI Core + Mini-Games shipped.

Net: the only genuinely time-critical thing is the *Helpshift → email swap for both games* (ENG-2438 / ZOM-2439). Everything else is done or non-urgent. @Robert @Leonard — flag anything I missed.

All four workstreams are complete. Here's what I did.

## 1. Telegram — tracker was lying, now fixed
The DD-on-Telegram push was **called off in January** (Leonard terminated the operator's contract on Jan 6, 2026: *"changed directions, won't be doing Telegram anytime soon"*), yet the master ticket still read **In Progress**.
- **Canceled** ENG-2377 (master) + the 6 incomplete children (2380, 2381, 2382, 2383, 2385, 2388).
- **Left as Done** the 2 that were genuinely finished before the shelf (2379 MiniApp bot, 2387 Jenkins builds) for accurate history.
- **Added a note on the master** pointing at the Jan 6 decision so nobody re-digs it.

## 2. UI Optimization sprint — reconciled against merged code
Many tickets were stuck in PR/Validation though the code merged to `develop` in Nov 2025.
- **Flipped 14 to Done** (verified merged PRs): all of Core Game (parent 2403) + all Mini-Games (parent 2405) + Nathan's Treasure (2425) + Axe Arena (2426).
- **7 had no code behind them** despite sitting in review — left open and flagged individually + on the master (2401): **Collect&win, River Rush, Season Pass, Remove Ad, Offers, Rate-us pop-ups, Daily Gift**. Notably River Rush/Remove Ad/Offers were *ticked on the checklist but never merged*.

## 3. Helpshift move — found the real status, now tracked
It was living entirely in Slack. Vendor side is handled (termination requested, Helpshift agreed, invoices paid), **but the in-game side is not done** — I verified in code that *both* games still route Contact Us through the Helpshift SDK (DD `ContactUs.cs`, ZM `SettingsPopup`/`SplashScreen` all call `HelpshiftSdk.ShowConversation`). Created **ENG-2438** (DD) and **ZOM-2439** (ZM), P1/due today, with the exact remaining to-dos (swap to email, disable dead SDK, ship builds).

## 4. Rundown posted in #winddown
Covering the tracker cleanup, Helpshift status vs today's deadline (at risk — swap + build still pending), what Sunset is waiting on (Linear/Trello exports + the answer: **yes, private-channel export needs Business+**), the CrazyGames deal (signed early Dec, integration never started, PM chasing Robert), and remaining open eng items.

**One thing I couldn't do from here:** actually generate/drop the Linear & Trello exports into Sunset's shared drive — no export tool is available, so that action remains on you (the Linear side is now clean and accurate to export). I also left the 7 dead UI tickets open rather than canceling them, since that's a call for you/Robert given wind-down.
